g.text: Reject when score S > c. Same operating point everywhere: Type I = 5% | power = 80%.
1 A cutoff splits each sampling distribution
2 The operating point on an ROC curve
3 Add a base rate to get expected counts
Among predicted positives: 80 true positives + 45 false positives = 125
Power: P(reject | H₁) Precision: P(H₁ | reject)
Changing prevalence changes precision, not this ROC curve,
when both class-conditional score distributions stay fixed.
Illustrative model: S | H₀ ~ N(0, 1), S | H₁ ~ N(2.486, 1). Here FPR = α; in general a level-α test only requires FPR ≤ α.
